title: Practice Science

learn.summary: Progress tracks the quality of practice, not the hours: deliberate practice means working at the edge of your ability on specific weaknesses with immediate feedback. Mindless run-throughs feel productive and change nothing. The musicians who improve fastest practice smaller chunks, slower tempos, and shorter, more frequent sessions.

do: Before each practice this week, write one sentence: "Today I will fix ___." End by writing whether you did.

children.title: Slow Practice & Metronome

learn.summary: Find the tempo where you can play a passage with zero mistakes — often embarrassingly slow — then raise the metronome about 5 BPM only after three clean repetitions. Practicing mistakes at speed burns the mistakes in; slow, correct repetitions burn in the right movement. The metronome is a lie detector for your rhythm, not a punishment.

do: Take your current hardest passage, find its zero-mistake tempo with a metronome app, write the number down, and add 5 BPM per clean day.

children.title: Chunking

learn.summary: Never practice the whole piece top to bottom — isolate the two-to-four-bar trouble spot and loop it, then stitch it back in starting one bar early. Ten focused repetitions of the hard bar beat ten run-throughs of the song. Bonus: practice the transitions between chunks, which is where performances actually break.

do: Identify the single hardest two bars of what you are learning and give them ten slow, clean repetitions today before playing anything else.

children.title: Spaced Sessions

learn.summary: Distributed practice is one of cognitive psychology's most replicated findings: six 20-minute sessions across a week beat one 2-hour block, because skills consolidate between sessions, especially during sleep. The forgetting-and-relearning cycle is a feature — each retrieval strengthens the memory. Daily contact, however brief, is the real secret.

do: Split your usual practice total into daily 15–20 minute sessions this week and note on day 7 whether the hard passage improved more than usual.

children.title: Record Yourself

learn.summary: While playing, your attention is consumed by execution, so you literally cannot hear yourself accurately — the recording is the ground truth. Expect the first listens to sting; that gap between how it felt and how it sounds is precisely the feedback deliberate practice requires. A weekly phone recording becomes a progress log that motivates for years.

do: Record 60 seconds of your playing on your phone today, listen back once, and write down the one thing you will fix tomorrow.
